findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are disabled on first login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` returns true only when `user != null`. In `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137) it is called with `context.getUser()`, which is null on a fresh login. As a result `fillContextForm` is never called for unauthenticated users. Conditional-UI passkey login on the initial username/password page is lost, which is the main passkeys scenario; previously that case was explicitly supported. The condition looks inverted or misplaced: it should probably not depend on the user at all.

findings.title: No-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() call doesn't match the defined overload
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method added in `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, so this either fails to compile or depends on an overload that isn't shown. Even if it is changed to pass `context.getUser()`, the semantics differ from the intended check of whether passkeys are enabled.
